note: Each question: options[], answer = index of the correct option. diagram (optional): p=[label,x,y,team u|o] in feet (rink 85x200, goal at top), k=puck, g=goalie team, c=caption.

questions.text: F1 has the puck in the corner with a defender (X1) closing in. F3 is wide open in the slot. What is the best play?
options: Shoot from the corner at a tiny angle
Pass to F3 in the slot
Dump the puck out of the zone
questions.why: The slot is the best scoring area, and F3 is open. A pass to open ice beats a shot from a bad angle.

diagram.c: Gold = your team, attacking the net at the top.

questions.text: D1 has the puck at the blue line and is about to shoot. F1 is in the high slot. What should F1 do?
options: Get to the front of the net (not in the crease) to screen the goalie and look for a rebound
Stand still in the high slot
Go behind the net and wait
questions.why: Screens and rebounds score a lot of goals. Get in front of the goalie’s eyes, but stay out of the crease.

diagram.c: D1 has the puck at the left point.

questions.text: You are F1 on a 2-on-1. The only defender (X1) is staying right next to F2 to block the pass. What should F1 do?
options: Dump the puck into the corner
Shoot, or drive to the net
questions.why: The defender chose to cover F2, so the shot is open. Make the defender pay for it.

questions.text: A teammate takes a shot and the goalie makes a save, but the puck pops loose. Where should you be?
options: Skating toward the net, ready for the rebound
Standing still and watching the shot
questions.why: Most rebound goals go to the player who is already moving to the net.

questions.text: F1 passes the puck to F2 along the boards. What should F1 do next?
options: Skate to open ice to give F2 a passing option
Skate to the blue line and stop
questions.why: Pass, then move. Moving creates new passing options and keeps the cycle going.

diagram.c: F1 has the puck and is about to pass up the boards to F2.

questions.text: The puck is on the left side of the zone and you are the winger on the far (weak) side. What is your best spot?
options: An open spot near the far post, ready for a pass or rebound
In the corner with the puck carrier
questions.why: Weak-side players slide to open ice near the net, where a cross-ice pass or rebound can come.

questions.text: F2 is already in the offensive zone. F1 is still in the neutral zone carrying the puck toward the blue line. What happens if F1 crosses the blue line?
options: Offside: the whistle blows and play stops
questions.why: The puck must cross the blue line before the attackers do. F2 should have waited for the puck or come back onside.

diagram.c: The blue line is at y = 75 ft. F2 is past it; the puck is not.

questions.text: X1 has the puck in the corner and X2 is alone in the slot. D1 is on X1. Who should cover X2 in front of your net?
options: F3, who is up near the blue line
D2, who is closest to X2
questions.why: The closest defender covers the slot. D1 handles the puck, D2 handles the front of the net.

diagram.c: You are defending the net at the top.

questions.text: X1 is about to shoot from the point. F1 is high on that side. What should F1 do?
options: Turn away so you do not get hit
Get a stick and body in the shooting lane to block it
questions.why: Block the lane and the goalie can see the shot. Shot lanes are part of defending.

diagram.c: X1 has the puck at the left point.

questions.text: You win the puck in your own zone along the boards. What is the best play?
options: Look up and make a safe pass up the boards
Pass across the middle in front of your own net
Shoot it at your own goalie
questions.why: A cross-ice pass in front of your net can be stolen and turn into a goal against.

questions.text: X2 is standing in front of your net while the puck is at the point. What should D2 do?
options: Chase the puck carrier at the point
Leave and go to the bench
Tie up X2’s stick and box him out
questions.why: Stop him from tipping the shot or taking the rebound. Stick on stick, body between him and the puck.

questions.text: Your team loses the puck in the offensive zone and the other team starts up the ice. What does your forward do?
options: Stay up high waiting for a pass
Hustle back and cover the closest opponent
questions.why: Backchecking helps your defense. The play changes the moment the puck changes teams.

questions.text: You are D1, the only defender back against a 2-on-1. What is best?
options: Chase the puck carrier and leave the other player open
Stay between them, stick in the passing lane, and make the puck carrier shoot
questions.why: You cannot cover both players, so take away the pass and let the goalie handle the shot.

diagram.c: X1 has the puck. You are D1.

questions.text: Offensive-zone faceoff. F1 wins the draw straight back. Who is best set up to receive it?
options: D1, lined up on the puck side
Nobody: it is a free puck
questions.why: The strong-side defenseman should be ready for the draw back and shoot or pass.

questions.text: Who may be inside the faceoff circle when the puck is dropped?
questions.why: Everyone else stays outside the circle until the puck is dropped.

questions.text: Your team loses a faceoff in your own zone. What is everyone’s first job?
options: Cover your man and get between the puck and your net
questions.why: Do not all chase the puck. Cover your player first, then help win it back.

questions.text: A teammate shoots the puck from behind center ice all the way past the opponents’ goal line and nobody touches it. What is the call?
questions.why: The puck crossed both the center red line and the goal line untouched, so it is icing and the faceoff comes back to your zone.

questions.text: You are on the bench waiting for a line change. When is it safe to go on?
options: When your teammate is close to the bench and about to come off
Right away, even if he is far away
When he is in the corner with the puck
questions.why: Too many men on the ice is a penalty. Wait until your teammate is close and the play is not near you.

questions.text: Your team is ahead by one goal with one minute left. What is the best play?
options: Try a fancy move in front of your own net
Play smart: get the puck out and avoid risky passes
questions.why: Protect the lead with safe, simple plays. Clear the puck and keep moving.

questions.text: You carry the puck up the ice with your head down while a defender closes in. What should you do?
options: Skate faster with your head down
Keep your head up and look for an open teammate
questions.why: Head up means you can see passing options and defenders before it is too late.
